title: Rethinking in Spikes: Mitigating Hallucinations in MDLMs with Step-Aware Decoding
claim: Sudden local uncertainty spikes during iterative generation coincide with erroneous content and can be detected as deviations from the local trend.
layout: 3 panels: example on top, two plots below; orange spikes link to text
description: Panel (a), across the top, shows a user prompt 'Describe this image in detail.' beside a photo of a road-maintenance truck and workers at a zebra crossing. To the right is the model's long caption highlighted in blue shades, with some phrases in orange (e.g. 'upright cone-shaped roadwork marker', 'A long metal rail extends') marking hallucinated content. Dashed orange arrows link these phrases to red tick marks on a denoising-step timeline from T to 0, labeled 'Entropy Spikes'. Panel (b), bottom left, is a blue bar chart of mean entropy against step (0–256) with a smooth falling curve and a zoomed inset showing red-dot spikes. Panel (c), bottom right, is a line plot of stepwise Δ entropy with a red dashed μ+σ bound and red dots where the line exceeds it.
caption: Entropy spikes in denoising dynamics. (a) A representative example illustrating the correlation between entropy spikes and hallucinations. Tokens committed at steps with an entropy spike closely correspond to hallucinated content in the response. (b) Mean mask entropy decreases steadily across denoising, while a few steps show sharp rises that break the local trend, which we refer to as entropy spikes. (c) A step is flagged as an entropy spike when its stepwise entropy change exceeds the µ + σ bound from the calibration window.
abstract: Recent advancements in multimodal diffusion language models (MDLMs) have exhibited strong global modeling capabilities through iterative refinement. We observe that mask uncertainty follows an overall downward trend during iterative denoising, while a few denoising steps exhibit localized entropy spikes closely associated with hallucinations. We argue that anomalous steps can be identified by measuring the entropy deviation of each denoising step from its neighboring temporal window. We hypothesize that discrete token commitment discards the distributional information at masked positions, limiting the continued interaction between candidate semantics and the context during entropy spikes. With this goal, we present StepRefine, a plug-and-play decoding strategy that leverages semantic context to achieve reliable denoising. The core of our method lies in a step-aware switch between discrete denoising and latent refinement. The model employs probability-weighted embeddings at entropy spike steps to preserve diverse reasoning hypotheses and performs multiple rounds of continuous refinement. Meanwhile, a refinement controller monitors distributional stability to reduce unnecessary loops and switch the model back to standard discrete denoising. Through extensive experiments, StepRefine demonstrates significant hallucination mitigation across different MDLMs on multimodal benchmarks.
